# Compile-Time (`#!`) and `Type` Reflection

Edva uses a unified compile-time evaluation and structural reflection model introduced by `#!` and the `Type` primitive. `Type` values, field cursors (`f`), and variant cursors (`v`) exist strictly at compile time and are erased before LLVM code generation with zero runtime footprint (`E2018` / `E3129`).

## Compile-time evaluation (`#!`) forms

| Construct | Syntax | Semantics | Diagnostic |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Compile-time expression** | `val = #! expr` | Evaluates pure expression `expr` during compilation and embeds the constant result | `E3129`: runtime-only op in `#!` |
| **Explicit `Type` parameter** | `f: #! T: Type => Int`<br>`f = #! T => #size T` | Specializes `f` per concrete `Type` passed at the call site (`f(Int)`) | `E2018`: `Type` used as runtime value |
| **Inferred `Type` parameter** | `f: #! T: Type, T => String`<br>`f = #! T, x => T.name` | Deduces `T` automatically from the runtime argument `x` (`f(42)` $\Rightarrow$ `T = Int`) | — |
| **Compile-time constant param** | `f: #! N: Int, Int => Int` | Specializes `f` on compile-time constant `N` | — |
| **Type generator** | `Pair: #! T: Type => (a: T, b: T)`<br>`#type IntPair Pair(Int)` | Compile-time function returning a composite `Type`, registered via `#type` | — |

```{.dva .run}
#use io

Pair: #! T: Type => (first: T, second: T)
#type IntPair Pair(Int)

fact: Int => Int
fact = n => n !> 1 | 1 | n * fact(n - 1)

f5 = #! fact(5)
p = IntPair(10, f5)
io::out $ (p.first, p.second)   // (10, 120)
```

## `Type` properties and compile-time intrinsics

Given `T: Type`, the compiler resolves the following properties as compile-time constants:

| Expression | Result Type | Specification |
|---|---|---|
| `#size T` | `Int` | Target ABI byte size of `T` |
| `#align T` | `Int` | Target ABI byte alignment of `T` |
| `T.name` | `String` | Declared `#type` alias name (if nominal) or canonical type name (`"Int"`, `"String"`, etc.) |
| `T.zero` | `T` | Default/zero-initialized value of `T` (respects `field: Type = default` on records) |
| `?T` | `Int` | Field count for records, lane count `N` for `(E * N)`, variant count for enums, `0` for `()` |
| `T.(i)` | `String` | Variant name of the `i`-th enum variant (`0 <= i < ?T`; `i` must be compile-time constant, `E3170`) |

```{.dva .run}
#use io

#type ServerCfg (host: String = "127.0.0.1", port: Int = 8080, tls: <>)
#type Mode < Fast, Safe >

cfg = ServerCfg.zero
io::out $ (ServerCfg.name, ?ServerCfg, cfg.host, cfg.port, Mode.(0), #size Int, #align Int)
```

## Structural type-shape guards (`T [...]`)

When the scrutinee of a choice is `T: Type`, the compiler resolves the matching branch at compile time, prunes all untaken branches before type-checking/codegen, and binds inner component types in the taken branch scope:

| Guard Pattern | Matched Type Shape | Bound `Type` Variables in Branch Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `[Int, i32]` | Exact type equality (comma OR-list) | — |
| `[type::is_numeric]` | Compile-time `Type => <>` predicate (`#use type`) | — |
| `[()]` | `Unit` (`()`) | — |
| `[<>]` or `[<|>]` | `Flag` (`<>`) | — |
| `[<P|>]` | `RamPN` option (`< P | >`) | `P`: positive payload `Type` |
| `[<|N>]` | `RamNP` fallible (`< | N >`) | `N`: negative payload `Type` |
| `[<P | N>]` | `RamPP` result (`< P | N >`) | `P`: positive `Type`, `N`: negative `Type` |
| `[E{}]` | Growable array (`E{}`) | `E`: element `Type` |
| `[E[]]` | Slice (`E[]`) | `E`: element `Type` |
| `[(E * ..)]` | Any homogeneous tuple (`(E * N)`) | `E`: element `Type` (`?T` gives length `N`) |
| `[(E * 4)]` | Homogeneous tuple of exact length `4` | `E`: element `Type` |
| `[K ^ V]` / `[String ^ V]` | Hash map (`K ^ V`) | `K`: key `Type`, `V`: value `Type` |
| `[(..)]` | Any record type | — (unroll fields with `T @ f =>`) |
| `[<..>]` | Any nominal enum type | — (unroll variants with `T @ v =>`) |

## Compile-time record field (`T @ f =>`) and enum variant (`T @ v =>`) unrolling

Inside a `#!` generic function, iterating over a record `Type` (`[(..)]`) or enum `Type` (`[<..>]`) with `@` unrolls the loop body at compile time across `0..?T`:

| Cursor Expression | Record Field Cursor (`T @ f =>`) | Enum Variant Cursor (`T @ v =>`) |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor.idx` | `Int`: `0`-based field index | `Int`: `0`-based variant tag index |
| `cursor.name` | `String`: field name (or `"0"`, `"1"` for tuples) | `String`: declared variant label (`"Red"`, etc.) |
| `cursor.type` | `Type`: static type of the field (`FT = f.type`) | `Type`: payload type, or `()` for unit variants |
| `f.default` | `< f.type | >`: `<+ default_val +>` if declared, else `<-->` | — |
| `val.(cursor)` | Reads field `f` from runtime record `val` (type `f.type`) | Returns `< v.type | >` (`<+ payload +>` / `<++>` if active tag is `v.idx`, else `<-->`) |
| `val'.(f) = expr` | Writes `expr` to field `f` of `val'` (tracks definite init) | — |
| `T(v)` / `T(v, p)` | — | Constructs runtime enum `T` for variant `v` |

```{.dva .run}
#use io
#use type

#type Point (x: Int = 1, y: Int = 2)
#type Shape < Dot, Circle(Int), Box(Int) >

inspect_record: #! T: Type, T => String
inspect_record = #! T, rec =>
   T
      [(..)]
         b = {64}
         b += T.name + "("
         T @ f =>
            f.idx > 0 | b += ","
            b += f.name + "=" + "${rec.(f)}"
         b += ")"
         +b
      | ""

enum_tag_name: #! T: Type, T => String
enum_tag_name = #! T, val =>
   T
      [<..>]
         b = {32}
         T @ v =>
            val.(v) | p =>
               b += v.name
         +b
      | ""

p = Point(10, 20)
s = Shape(Circle, 5)
io::out $ (inspect_record(p), enum_tag_name(s))
```

## Target compile-time variables (`os`, `arch`, `target`)

Inside `#! (...)` compile-time value and type expressions, the compiler exposes three built-in `String` variables derived from the active target triple (`--target <triple>`):

| Variable | Type | Values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `os` | `String` | `"linux"`, `"darwin"`, `"windows"`, `"freebsd"`, `"openbsd"`, `"netbsd"`, `"wasm"`, `"wasi"`, `"unknown"` | Normalized target operating system (`wasm32-unknown-unknown` $\Rightarrow$ `"wasm"`, `wasm32-wasi` $\Rightarrow$ `"wasi"`) |
| `arch` | `String` | `"x86_64"`, `"aarch64"`, `"x86"`, `"wasm32"`, ... | Normalized target CPU architecture (first segment of the target triple) |
| `target` | `String` | e.g. `"x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu"`, `"wasm32-unknown-unknown"` | Full target triple string |

Use `os`, `arch`, and `target` in `#! (...)` constant and `#type` choices to select platform-specific constants, struct layouts, or implementation branches without emitting dead host imports on inactive targets:

```{.dva .run}
#use io

CLOCK_MONOTONIC = #! (os ["darwin"] 6 ["wasm", "wasi"] 1 | 1)

#type PlatDarwin (darwin: Int, tag: Int)
#type PlatWasm   (wasm: Int, tag: Int)
#type PlatPosix  (posix: Int, tag: Int)
#type PlatTarget #! (os ["darwin", "freebsd", "openbsd", "netbsd"] PlatDarwin ["wasm", "wasi"] PlatWasm | PlatPosix)

platform_kind: #! P: Type => String
platform_kind = #! P =>
   P
      [PlatDarwin] "bsd-darwin"
      [PlatWasm]   "webassembly"
      |            "posix"

io::out $ (CLOCK_MONOTONIC, platform_kind(PlatTarget), #! arch)
```
